paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when God's grace shows up, you make room for it. Antioch begins with believers scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen (Acts 11:19). Some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, started "proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus" to the Greeks as well (Acts 11:20). "The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord" (Acts 11:21).

Now watch what the people around that grace do with it. Barnabas "saw the grace of God," and he "rejoiced" (Acts 11:23). He didn't hoard the work either. He went and got Saul, and together they taught large numbers of people. I think that's the real power move, friend: being glad about what God is doing, even when somebody else's name is on it, and then pulling in more help instead of guarding the job.

And when the news turned hard, with Agabus predicting a famine, the church in Antioch didn't hide in the cupboard. "Each according to his ability," they decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea (Acts 11:29). So ask yourself, baker: what's the grace in front of you, and who can you make room for or send help to today? Keep those ovens ready, because the Lord does the work, and He lets us take part in it.
